# ADDENDUM 23 — July 23 (evening) through July 27, 2026 — EFFECTOR COMPOSER SHIPPED, THE 9012/WEDGE FORENSICS, THE SHOP MOVE (AND THE ROUTER SAGA), J4 SOLVED WITH THE FLIGHT RECORDER, THE VISION RESET, THE CLOUD RECOGNITION PILOT
*(Appended in full. Nothing above this line was removed. This addendum spans four working days: the effector fix and controller forensics of July 23–24, the physical relocation to the Jade Group facility and its network saga of July 24–26, and the marathon July 27 session that closed the J4 wrist arc, reset the vision pipeline, and launched the cloud-trained recognition pilot.)*

### Section 387: Effector-aware composer SHIPPED (2ff0616) — Engage/Disengage vacuum

The §381 effector fix landed: composer emits **"Engage vacuum" / "Disengage vacuum"** step names for vacuum cells (operator-specified exact labels; no gripper verbs on vacuum cells), DO2 on/off + DO3 blow-off triplet on disengage, bound symmetrically through the io_map "Vacuum" assignment (one port source, never two hardcoded refs). A **server-side `/recompose` endpoint** rebuilds the draft deterministically from intent+answers; a "↻ Regenerate draft" button exposed it in the review UI. Verified via curl against the real black-bracket demo (16-step vacuum-shaped output). **55 pinned tests passing.** The root case ("said suction cup, got gripper") was confirmed: the intent stage had classified the effector correctly; the composer had no vacuum vocabulary to emit.

### Section 388: The 9012 postmortem — verdict (a), normal shutdown residue

Alarm 9012 "Power disconnection detected" blocked the morning of July 24. Full forensics: operator e-stopped at 17:40 the prior evening (alarm 2006, expected) → drives held open → DC bus bled through pre-charge resistors → 9012 at 17:56 (technically true, practically meaningless) → overnight hard power-down → the morning dashboard faithfully displayed yesterday's last state. **Verdict: normal end-of-day shutdown wearing an alarm banner.** Operator confirmed both the e-stop and the power-down were deliberate. Lesson: 9012 after e-stop + shutdown is expected residue. Backlog nicety: alarm modal should show the alarm's timestamp ("this happened 14 hours ago").

Also settled in the same forensics: the smoothing/blend prompt had correctly **STOPPED at its capture gate** — no wire-verified blend syntax exists in any captured program, so no codegen change shipped. Blend verbs formally joined the factory-UI capture-session shopping list. The executed Lua contained zero blend parameters; the motion-path changes were exonerated of the alarm.

### Section 389: Zombie boot #2 and the unclearable alarm

The alarm could not be cleared because **C2Control/projectlua never started on the morning boot** — network stack up (blue LED = standby/healthy), port 9000 connection-refused for hours, factory UI showing "Server network closed!" (its backend absent). Second consecutive cold boot to fail while the driver was reconnecting — and this one with the HARDENED driver (grace period, readiness probe, backoff), whose 07:10 log showed a brief connect dying with "no close frame" — suspiciously inside the init window. Recovery: the July 22 procedure, now rehearsed — `systemctl stop roboai-estun` → cold power cycle → `while true; do nc -zv -w 3 192.168.2.136 9000 && break; sleep 10; done` (timed out → connection refused → succeeded) → start driver. Open item: **driver boot-grace hardening** — gate the first WebSocket on a bare TCP probe succeeding, so the manual stop-boot-probe-start procedure becomes the driver's automatic behavior.

### Section 390: The wedge was REAL — controller held state=3 for 2h41m

The July 24 stop-wedge investigation (§ wedge banner work) concluded with hard evidence: at the 11:54:57 reconnect the controller pushed state 0→3 for `roboaihome` — it had been holding STOPPING since **09:13:38**, across an e-stop, jogging, and a driver restart. `project/stop` was sent once at 09:13:37; state 2→3 followed; **3→0 never came.** Genuine controller-side stop-completion failure (first program of the post-zombie-boot session — possibly boot residue), not lost frames. Shipped mitigations: **stop verification loop** (after our stop, poll the captured state-query verb 500ms×5s; if polling shows 0 but no push arrived, publish the corrected state and log 'stop completed; push frame lost' — measuring hypothesis-2 frequency for free) + **one automatic re-issue** of project/stop at 3s (bounded, logged — automating the manual Force-stop), banner copy now evidence-based ("stop sent twice, controller not confirming"). The negative-latency readout (−318ms) was traced to the cross-machine clock clamp **lost in the store.js→useStore.js migration** — monotonic/same-machine deltas restored; wedge claims now require FRESH contradicting frames (stale stream ≥3s gets its own neutral banner, never controller-blame). `ESTUN_DEBUG_STATE_DUMP=1` JSONL instrumentation added for the dual-observation session.

**Ledgered, still open:** the ACK-starved state channel — 3,892 ack_timeouts vs 200 acks_seen (~95% failure) — functioning by retry luck; visibly causing browser WS reconnect churn by July 27. Repair is the next infrastructure item. Also `cam0_live:false` intermittency noted alongside.

### Section 399: The Accept-binding disease — record vs apply, closed at the artifact

Operator answered "vacuum," pressed Accept, saved program still contained "Grip part" — screenshot showed the effector clarification ANSWERED (vacuum) with open_gripper steps rendered below it. Root cause: **draft restructuring only ran via the manual ↻ Regenerate button; Accept serialized the stale in-memory draft.** The third instance of the same disease (answered-state chip, surviving detect step, now this): *recording an answer and applying an answer are different operations, and every prior fix verified application in isolation while the binding stayed optional.*

Shipped/authored fixes, in order:
1. **Accept recomposes server-side, unconditionally** — the endpoint applies clarAnswers to intent, runs the deterministic compose, persists THAT; client renders the returned (actually-saved) program; pinned test = the exact operator scenario (answer vacuum → Accept without Regenerate → persisted program has Engage/Disengage vacuum, zero gripper steps) + the fixed-position variant. White-bowl program repair via recompose from stored intent+answers (before/after step list, no silent overwrite).
2. **Auto-recompose on every answer** — steps rebuild instantly on any clarification change (400ms debounce, seq-tagged stale-response guard, subtle busy state, changed-step amber flash — the causality made visible), previous draft kept on error, manual-edit clobber guard, ↻ button removed (Accept keeps its server recompose as belt-and-suspenders).
3. **Blow-off opt-in:** Disengage vacuum = vacuum-off only by default; blow-off gated on cell config `blow_off_enabled` (default false) + a review toggle flowing through the Accept binding; existing saved programs untouched; the 2ff0616 pinned test split into default/enabled variants. Physics note kept: light parts clinging to the cup is what blow-off exists for — config, not deletion.
4. **Draft-step deletion (prompt authored, pending):** deletions as an **exclusion overlay** keyed on deterministic step_keys so they survive auto-recompose; ghost rows with in-place Restore; anchor deletion greys+excludes dependents; Accept applies exclusions server-side; each exclusion lands in the learning record as a structured operator signal. Delete-only in review (authoring stays in the editor — no forked step-editing implementations).
5. **Full answer-path audit prompt:** every review control traced answer→intent→composer→SAVED artifact with a pinned test per control; learning records gain applied_rev/hash so recorded-but-not-applied is detectable in data forever.

### Section 401: J4 SOLVED — the flight recorder pays for itself

**The instrumentation (shipped July 27):** always-on joint flight recorder — 25Hz tee of the existing joint stream into segmented gzip JSONL under /opt/cobot/joint_history/ with hard retention budget (2GB/14-day cap enforced in the writer — the 100%-disk scar codified), run manifests on ProjectState transitions, `GET /api/runs`, `GET /api/runs/{id}/excursions` (per-step per-joint start/end/min/max/excursion, >10° intra-step flags), recorder failure isolated from the state pipeline. The one-shot `/api/estun/joint_log` (built earlier the same arc, self-tested against a rigged 40° swing) retained for high-rate targeted captures.

**The diagnosis (same day, zero new bench time):** 22 runs already indexed. The bowl program's approach step showed **J4 excursion 64.9°** (taught-consistent −80° vs controller-chosen −16°), TCP visibly sweeping — operator's exact observation. Root cause: the Fix-A-era fallback emitted **movJPose (pose-form verb)** for the approach — handing the controller's own IK the branch choice; Step 4's movJ(taught joints) then yanked it back. Excursion *between* steps of a pair, endpoints clean per-step: the smoking-gun signature. (Both prior theories — endpoint branch flip, movL singularity transit — were adjacent but wrong; the TCP-swings observation killed the movL theory since linear moves hold the TCP by contract.)

**The fix (shipped, same session):** **seeded IK at codegen** — damped-least-squares on the trusted URDF, seeded and branch-locked to the anchor's taught joints, 45°/wrist-axis rejection gate, deterministic (pinned test); every derived waypoint now emits **explicit joints in the taught branch** — the controller's solver never gets a vote. Loud fallback with validation warning on non-convergence (never a silent flipped branch); codegen validation rule: >15° wrist delta between consecutive waypoints flags. **Verified against recordings: J4 64.9° → 0.8°, J5 24.5° → 0.6°; the whole pair within ~1.5° of taught configuration.**

**Open follow-up (prompt authored):** the descend-to-contact segments still emit the pose-form verb — measured clean in all recorded runs (tiny Z-only delta biases the solver near), but same exposed class; follow-up converts them (seeded endpoint joints + movL path where wire-verified, 15° endpoint check, zero pose-form verbs remaining in derived/contact motion), verified against the operator's next normal run via the recorder.

### Section 402: The vision reset — the detection math never degraded

Operator: "part recognition needs to be like when we first started" — with photographic evidence (the original RoboAi-era view: every object boxed, tight wireframe OBBs, distance/size/yaw, **no identity claims**). The operator's June-5 regression memory is literally recorded in §276.

**Git archaeology findings (decisive):** the core detection functions — segmentation, mask cleaning, clustering, OBB fit, temporal filter — are **MD5-identical from June 2 to HEAD.** The codebase grew 1,994 → 5,243 lines (37 net-new functions), all identity-layer. Two real regressions: (1) **the identity stack ran on every frame regardless of mode** — "All Objects" was matching-and-hiding, not skipping (per-frame template×library cost burned for nothing); (2) **the renderer was swapped** — the June-2 renderer drew steady wireframes+labels from the smoothed OBB; the HEAD renderer chased raw silhouettes and collapsed to grey boxes + stray contour squiggles without identity output. *The visible degradation was substantially the drawing, not the detecting.* Commit f598691 ("Restore June-5-equivalent scoring weights") proved the known-good landmark had been recognized and missed once before.

**Shipped:** June-2 renderer restored (dist-colored wireframes, arrow, label format — now drawing from EMA-smoothed values, steadier than June ever was) + the matcher hard-gated out of All Objects mode; post-June-2 detection improvements (min_depth, mask closing, EMA tracker) retained; yaw normalized to ±180° (the +570° label bug). Decision recorded: baseline 18b35ae philosophy (cleanest ancestor; layers re-enter only through A/B evidence), **freeze** — the classical pipeline is the bridge, not the product.

**The remaining failure is upstream of all code:** post-restore, phantoms still cluster on the glossy table's glare (specular stereo garbage → degenerate OBBs/spaghetti wireframes) and flat ~3mm cardboard stays invisible (inside the D435i's noise floor at 0.5m). Honest three-layer framing recorded: (1) worst-case scene physics (dark gloss + flat objects vs stereo depth); (2) possible config drift (D435i preset/decimation/exposure — unaudited since the move); (3) the structural truth — **depth segmentation measures height, it does not perceive; a height sensor is not an eye.** Operator's counter ("we detected exactly this before June") accepted as evidence that config/half-res changes cost real capability — the **depth-frame diagnostic prompt** (raw depth over glare/cardboard/table with numbers, active D435i config dump vs June launch files, offline stage-by-stage segmentation trace, degenerate-cluster 3D dump) is authored and PENDING; the delrin-on-the-clean-side 30-second test and a matte work surface are the standing zero-code actions.

### Section 404: The cloud recognition pilot — rented, scoped, launched

Simulation tiers laid out: (1) the CPU synthetic scene generator (June prompt, status unconfirmed); (2) **program dry-run against the digital twin** (cheap, all pieces exist — offered as a build prompt); (3) full Isaac Sim — RTX-gated as decided in June, but the URDF blocker has since cleared. **Cloud pricing researched July 27:** RTX 4090 median ~$0.39/hr (market down ~39% since July 2025); RunPod $0.34 Community / **$0.69 Secure** (chosen — data-sovereignty posture), per-second billing; L40S ~$1.56/hr if 24GB constrains. Buy-vs-rent: ownership wins only above ~40–50% utilization — months away.

**The pilot (bundle prompt authored):** one real part (delrin-class) → BlenderProc domain-randomized rendering (2,000 labeled 640px images: random poses/lighting/backgrounds/distractors, YOLO labels from ground truth, contact-sheet QA) → YOLOv8 fine-tune (best.pt + ONNX for Jetson inference) → **eval against 20–30 operator phone photos of the real part on the real bench** (the honest headline number). pod_setup.sh + runbook with the STOP-THE-POD checklist; nothing sensitive in the bundle (part mesh only). Cost estimate ~$2–4. Success framing: synthetic-only at 80–90% on real images proves CAD-in→detector-out; lower teaches which domain gap bites. **Strategic shape recorded: this detector is the successor to the entire classical identity pile — sensor-agnostic (works on D435i now, MotionCam later), and "customer emails a STEP file, by morning the cell recognizes the part" is the recognition version of the PBD thesis.** Cloud trains; Jetson runs.

**MotionCam "key to success?" — honest tripod answer recorded:** yes for sensing (0.52mm PSL vs the D435i's failure modes; the patent moat through ~2035; the camera-not-the-robot critical-path framing holds), no as sufficiency (§38's bin-picking-stays-hard verdict stands: recognition-in-clutter, grasping, bin motion planning, the long tail). Success = sensor (MotionCam, unordered, ARM64-driver email still the #1 pre-purchase unknown) + recognition intelligence (PPF/ICP stack + the learned detector now in flight) + the autonomy layer (the actual differentiation). Purchase stays on the autonomy timeline — today's D435i pain is prototype pain; a matte mat is not a $20K decision.

### Section 406: I/O evolution — proposal withdrawn, improvements chosen

Usage-aware auto-allocation ("start at next open port") was designed — with the critical correction that **ports map to wiring, not programs** (same function → same io_map port always; only genuinely-new functions get next-free) — then **withdrawn by the operator in favor of the current model.** The improvement list produced instead, two selected and prompted:
1. **I/O wire-verification flow** (prompt authored): guided per-port check on the I/O page — outputs pulsed through the gated write path with operator physical confirmation, inputs auto-confirmed on edge within a 10s window; results persisted per assignment with ✓/✗/— badges; staleness at 30 days or on-edit invalidation; refuses unless idle; air-must-be-connected intro per the click≠shift lesson. Converts the relay-saga hardware lessons into a permanent tool.
2. **verify_input step** (prompt authored): post-action sensor confirmation — {DI, expect, timeout, on_fail: abort|retry_once|continue}; abort surfaces a stated reason in the dashboard AND the run record (manifest gains fail-reason); composer auto-emits a vacuum-seal verify after Engage vacuum **iff** a "Vacuum sensor" DI is named in io_map (never invents ports); wait_input gains timeout+branch. The pick-that-knows-it-failed feature. Hardware note: a ~$20 vacuum switch teed into the suction line is the prerequisite for auto-confirm — added to the parts list if not present.

Also: phone dashboard access documented (same https://192.168.1.143:8080 on shop Wi-Fi; phone = glance-and-check screens); CTO pitch brief delivered (demo-shaped claim, data-flywheel + driver-library moat, autonomy staircase, the Standard Bots answer, named-risks-with-mitigations, the one number: $1M for 10%).

## PROCESS LESSONS (132–142)

132. **Check the physical layer before the protocol layer.** A dark switch-port LED and a second power button explained hours of network-shaped symptoms. Cable seated? Port lit? Device actually powered? — before any command runs twice.
133. **`teddy-desktop.local` is the address-proof door.** mDNS by hostname survives every DHCP surprise; it would have worked at any moment after the Wi-Fi join, no monitor, no router page, no address hunt.
134. **The ISP owns the gateway — call first, not last.** An ISP-managed router's admin credential may exist only in their provisioning system; the router's own recovery dialog is who tells people to paperclip-reset; and re-provisioning restores THEIR records, not your install sheet.
135. **Stale static addresses are landmines.** The laptop's leftover 192.168.1.50 (July 8) silently misrouted every 2.x packet at the new shop and manufactured false "connection refused" evidence for an hour. Revert temporary network configs the same day they stop being needed.
136. **Label the machine; never put placeholders in code blocks.** Jetson commands were run on the laptop repeatedly, and example text (`<that-number>`, "YourHotspotName") was typed literally. Standing protocol: [JETSON]/[LAPTOP] tags on every command, literal copy-paste-ready text only.
137. **Recording an answer and applying it are different operations — bind at the artifact.** Three instances of the same disease (answered-state chip, surviving detect step, vacuum-answer-not-applied) all verified the application path while the binding stayed optional. Accept recomposes unconditionally; pinned tests assert on the PERSISTED program, the only place truth lives.
138. **Instrumentation before theory.** The J4 bug survived two theory passes and died in one data pass — because the flight recorder existed before the third question was asked. "Can we go back and look?" should always be answerable yes; the excursion table turned a debate into a lookup.
139. **Pose-form verbs give the controller a vote.** movJPose/movL hand the branch choice to the controller's IK; explicit seeded taught-branch joints remove the solver's discretion entirely. Endpoints correct is not enough — the path between them is where unmodeled configuration changes live.
140. **The detection math never degraded — the renderer was the regression.** MD5-identical core functions since June 2; the visible decline was a swapped overlay renderer plus an identity stack burning every frame. Presence and identity are different products; measure the layer you're actually judging.
141. **A height sensor is not an eye.** Depth segmentation measures elevation above a plane; it has no objectness. Flat objects on glossy dark tables are its structural blind spot — matte surfaces and real-height parts for the classical pipeline, learned RGB perception (the funded pilot) for everything it cannot see.
142. **Cloud trains, Jetson runs.** At $0.35–0.70/hr for a 4090, the entry cost to GPU training is an evening's coffee money; ownership wins only past ~40–50% utilization. The proprietary dataset goes to Secure-tier instances only, artifacts come home, and the pod gets STOPPED.

---

*Summary of Addendum 23: four days that closed three long arcs and opened the learned-perception era. The effector composer shipped (Engage/Disengage vacuum, the recompose endpoint) and then had to be finished properly when the operator proved answers weren't binding at Accept — the third instance of the record-vs-apply disease, now closed at the artifact with server-side recompose, auto-rebuilding drafts, and pinned tests on the persisted program. The 9012 alarm was forensically demoted to shutdown residue, the second zombie boot was survived by the rehearsed recovery, and the stop-wedge was proven a genuine controller hold (2h41m in state 3) — answered with a verification loop, a bounded auto-retry, and honest banners, while the 95%-ACK-timeout state channel moved up the queue. The cell moved to the Jade Group facility: the network transplanted intact once a stale laptop static, an un-elevated PowerShell, a second power button, and a dark switch LED were each run to ground — and the router saga (isolation, a locked ISP gateway, the paperclip reset the router itself instructed, self-re-provisioning) ended with the old credentials working and a lessons section heavier on humility than code. J4 was solved on the third pass because the flight recorder existed before the question — 64.9° of controller-chosen wrist swing traced to a pose-form verb and eliminated to 0.8° with seeded branch-locked IK. The vision saga resolved into its honest shape: the detection math never degraded (MD5-identical since June 2), the renderer and an always-running identity stack were the regression — restored and gated — while the remaining failures (glare phantoms, invisible cardboard) belong to physics and possibly config, with the depth-frame diagnostic authored and the real successor already funded: a $0.69/hr RTX 4090 rendering domain-randomized training data for the detector that will see what a height sensor never could. Fixed-cam vision-guided picking got its full prompt set (AprilTag extrinsic with a permanent drift-guard tag, snapshot-at-run pick_at_detection), I/O grew a wire-truth verification flow and a pick-that-knows-it-failed verify step, positions became first-class linked objects that sync across devices, and the repo's stale main was caught before it could hand anyone else a two-week-old photograph. Eleven lessons, one flight recorder, and the first bug in project history solved entirely from data that existed before the theory did.*
